# /agents/

Agent Skills are task-specific, progressively disclosed instructions distributed with this repository. They complement the API docs by encoding source inspection, decision flow, invariants, security boundaries, verification, and handoff requirements that are easy for an agent to get wrong during implementation.



    Seven Skills cover manager design, custom checks, diagnostics security, cgroups, exporters, Next.js routes, and Payload integration.


    Four Skills cover semantic factories, managed slugs, Jalali dates, and minor-unit money contracts.


    Three Skills cover core semantic configuration, preset contracts, and native Payload extensions.


    Two Skills separate entity consumption and migration from package compiler, adapter, and release development.



## Use the smallest relevant skill

Install a Skill when the task matches its trigger. For example, install `healthcheck-nextjs-routes` when adding a Next App Router health route, not the entire collection by default.

Every Skill is self-contained for its primary task. A sibling Skill may be recommended for composition, but the primary workflow does not depend on reading it. Committed behavior evals cover a happy path, edge case, security/failure case, diagnosis/review case, and a near-miss or composition boundary; trigger evals balance 10 positive and 10 neighboring negative queries.

---

# /agents/install/

The repository ships 16 validated, self-contained Skills. The official `skills` CLI discovers the `skills/**/SKILL.md` files and configures them for supported agents. Each Skill keeps its core workflow in `SKILL.md`, routes deeper package contracts through `references/`, and commits behavior plus trigger cases under `evals/`.



1. Inspect the available Skills before installing:

   ```bash
   npx skills add gecut/nexload-sdk --list
   ```

2. Install a specific Skill for the current project:

   ```bash
   npx skills add gecut/nexload-sdk --skill healthcheck-core
   ```

3. Update installed Skills when you intentionally want newer guidance:

   ```bash
   npx skills update
   ```

Run `pnpm skills:validate` in a repository checkout to verify frontmatter, path/name consistency, references, line limits, behavior evals, and balanced trigger evals.

# /community/support/

Use GitHub Issues as the single public channel for bugs, documentation corrections, and feature requests.

<p>Open an issue</p>

## Report a useful issue

- Name the package and installed version.
- Include the smallest reproduction or the exact documentation page.
- State runtime and framework details when relevant.
- Remove tokens, connection strings, cookies, and production payloads.


Use the “Edit this page” link on any page when the correction is local to that document. Source behavior still takes priority over prose when they conflict.

# /index/

Nexload SDK is a collection of focused TypeScript packages for backend and platform work. Install only the package that owns your problem; packages do not require a framework-wide runtime.

## Start with a production concern



    Build liveness, readiness, startup, diagnostics, metrics, and framework route integrations without coupling the core to a single runtime.


    Add managed Unicode slugs, Jalali date UI, and integer minor-unit money contracts to Payload CMS.


    Give supported coding agents package-specific guardrails for health checks and Payload field conventions.



## Documented packages



## How the docs are organized

---

# /packages/healthcheck/concepts/checks-and-collectors/

Checks contribute a status to the report. Collectors add metrics and resources without independently changing the health status.



    ```ts
    import { shutdownCheck } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck";

    health.register(shutdownCheck());
    ```


    ```ts
    import { processMetricsCollector } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-node";

    health.registerCollector(processMetricsCollector());
    ```



## Choose deliberately

- Use a check when its status should affect a liveness, readiness, startup, or diagnostics report.
- Use a collector when telemetry is useful but should not change traffic or lifecycle decisions.
- Return raw metric values: number, boolean, string, or `null`.
- Keep `check.metrics` as JSON/report diagnostics. Prometheus and OpenTelemetry custom series come only from collector-produced `report.metrics`.


Use `defineHealthCheck` and honour the supplied `AbortSignal`. Thrown errors and timeouts are normalized into stable result entries; do not intentionally throw formatted user-facing errors from a check.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/concepts/reports-and-status/

Every run produces a `HealthReport` with service identity, scope, status, observation time, duration, runtime identity, check results, summary, metrics, and optional resources.

## Aggregation

| Check outcome | Critical | Aggregate outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unhealthy` | yes | `unhealthy` |
| `degraded` | yes | `degraded` |
| `unhealthy` | no | `degraded` by default |
| `ok` | any | no degradation |

The default HTTP policy maps `ok` and `degraded` to `200`, and `unhealthy` to `503`. Use `STRICT_READINESS_HTTP_STATUS_POLICY` or a custom `HealthHttpStatusPolicy` when your load balancer must treat degraded readiness as unavailable.

## Profiles and JSON serialization

Profiles are context hints passed to checks and collectors. They do not automatically filter checks, details, or metrics from a response.

Use `toHealthJson` or `stringifyHealthJson` to serialize a report. Details, original error messages, causes, and stacks are suppressed by default. Public routes should keep those defaults; diagnostics can opt into the minimum required fields only after route protection has been applied. Manager-level `redaction` and run-level `includeDiagnostics` remain deprecated compatibility fields and do not control serialization.


Redaction reduces accidental disclosure in report data. It does not make a diagnostics endpoint public-safe. Keep the route protected as well.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/concepts/scopes/

Healthcheck scopes answer different questions. A check can participate in more than one scope, but each placement should match a real operational decision.


  Should this process keep running? Use lifecycle and event-loop signals, not ordinary remote dependencies.
  Should this instance receive traffic? Put required dependencies and capacity thresholds here.
  Has initialisation completed? Use it while the process is not yet safe to serve.
  What does an operator need to inspect? Keep it detail-rich and protected.


## Default probe posture

| Scope | Typical route | Detail level | Default failure behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `liveness` | `/health/live` | minimal | restart only for process lifecycle failure |
| `readiness` | `/health/ready` | minimal | remove from traffic |
| `startup` | `/health/startup` | minimal | wait before routing traffic |
| `diagnostics` | private route | rich | operator investigation only |


Diagnostics may contain failure context and resource data. Protect it with authentication, private networking, IP policy, or a reverse proxy. Never expose secrets, connection strings, headers, cookies, or stack traces.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/guides/bun/

The Bun adapter reports Bun runtime information and can collect basic `Bun.serve` server metrics. It does not depend on the Node adapter.





1. Supply `bunRuntimeAdapter()` to the manager.

   ```ts
   import { createHealthManager, shutdownCheck } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck";
   import { bunRuntimeAdapter, bunServerMetricsCheck } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-bun";

   const server = Bun.serve({ fetch: () => new Response("ok") });

   export const health = createHealthManager({
     service: { name: "bun-api" },
     runtime: bunRuntimeAdapter(),
     checks: [shutdownCheck(), bunServerMetricsCheck(server)],
   });
   ```

2. Keep Bun-only checks behind the Bun integration boundary.




The Bun adapter uses available process memory APIs. It does not claim host or cgroup memory limits that Bun cannot provide.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/guides/custom-checks/

Use `defineHealthCheck` for a status-bearing probe and `defineMetricCollector` for monitoring-only collection.

```ts

export const licenseCheck = defineHealthCheck({
  name: "license",
  scopes: ["readiness", "diagnostics"],
  critical: true,
  timeoutMs: 1_000,
  async run(ctx) {
    const valid = await verifyLicense({ signal: ctx.signal });

    return {
      status: valid ? "ok" : "unhealthy",
      metrics: { valid },
      error: valid ? undefined : {
        code: "LICENSE_INVALID",
        message: "License is not valid.",
      },
    };
  },
});
```

## Custom check rules

- Honour `ctx.signal`; timeout is cooperative and ignored cancellation can leak or overlap work during retries.
- Use stable machine-readable error codes.
- Return raw numbers, booleans, strings, or `null` as metrics.
- Keep high-cardinality or sensitive values out of metrics, labels, details, resources, and errors. Profiles are context hints, not automatic response filters.


The manager converts thrown errors, timeouts, and aborts into check results. Let unexpected failures be unexpected; do not throw as a normal status transport.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/guides/exporters/

The exporter packages transform an already-created `HealthReport`. They do not run checks and do not require an OpenTelemetry SDK.





    ```ts
    import { toPrometheusText } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-prometheus";

    const text = toPrometheusText(report, {
      prefix: "nexload",
      defaultLabels: { service: "api" },
      includeDescriptions: true,
    });
    ```


    ```ts
    import {
      toOtelMetricRecords,
      toOtelResourceAttributes,
    } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-otel";

    const metrics = toOtelMetricRecords(report);
    const resource = toOtelResourceAttributes(report);
    ```



Custom exporter metrics come from collectors in `report.metrics`; raw `check.metrics` stays in JSON/report diagnostics. Prometheus drops labels outside its controlled allowlist and emits `# HELP` for built-ins and described collector metrics when `includeDescriptions` is enabled. OpenMetrics adds the `# EOF` terminator.


Prometheus output accepts only a controlled label set. OTel record conversion copies labels verbatim and does not sanitize or bound cardinality. Never use user IDs, request IDs, raw URLs, raw error messages, tokens, or stack traces as labels.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/guides/nextjs/

Use the Next integration to turn a manager into `GET` and `HEAD` handlers. Routes with process or container checks must use the Node runtime and remain uncached.





- src
  - app
    - api
      - health
        - ready
          - route.ts
  - lib
    - health.ts





1. Export an initialized manager from a server-only module.

2. Create a readiness route.

   ```ts title="src/app/api/health/ready/route.ts"
   import { createNextHealthRoute } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-next";
   import { health } from "@/lib/health";

   export const runtime = "nodejs";
   export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
   export const revalidate = 0;
   export const fetchCache = "force-no-store";

   export const { GET, HEAD } = createNextHealthRoute(health, {
     scope: "readiness",
     format: "json",
   });
   ```

3. Use `createNextMetricsRoute` for Prometheus, OpenMetrics, or JSON monitoring output.



Use `STRICT_READINESS_HTTP_STATUS_POLICY` when degraded readiness must return `503`; the default policy returns `200` for degraded and `503` only for unhealthy. Metrics routes always return HTTP `200` and expose report state through `x-health-status`.


Use the `protect` option for bearer tokens, Basic auth, IPv4 allowlists, or IPv4 CIDRs. Empty protection and credentials are configuration errors. IP/CIDR rules require `trustProxy: true`; missing or invalid forwarded addresses fail closed with `401`. Set proxy trust only when the deployment overwrites the configured header. Every success and denial response remains `no-store`.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/guides/node/

Use the Node adapter when your service needs process metrics, cgroup-aware container data, TCP checks, or DNS checks.





1. Configure the Node runtime adapter.

   ```ts title="src/lib/health.ts"
   import { createHealthManager, shutdownCheck } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck";
   import {
     nodeRuntimeAdapter,
     processMetricsCollector,
     tcpCheck,
   } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-node";

   export const health = createHealthManager({
     service: { name: "api" },
     runtime: nodeRuntimeAdapter(),
     checks: [shutdownCheck(), tcpCheck("postgres", { host: "db", port: 5432 })],
     collectors: [processMetricsCollector()],
   });
   ```

2. Add `containerResourceCheck` only when memory or CPU pressure should influence a health decision.



## Container data

`containerResourceCheck` reads cgroup v2, then cgroup v1. Fractional CPU quotas are preserved; unlimited sentinels remain `null`, not zero. Inspect source, confidence, and warnings before using a metric as a hard threshold. Process/host memory fallback belongs to `nodeRuntimeAdapter`, not the raw container snapshot.


`processMetricsCollector` and `containerMetricsCollector` are suitable for metrics routes. They do not turn a service unhealthy by themselves.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/guides/operations/

Healthcheck works in containers without assuming that host memory or CPU is the process limit. The Node adapter checks cgroup v2 and v1 before lower-confidence fallbacks.

## Probe mapping

| Platform concern | Scope | Expected action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| process is shutting down | `liveness` and `readiness` | stop new traffic; allow shutdown |
| required dependency is unavailable | `readiness` | remove instance from traffic |
| application initialisation is incomplete | `startup` | wait before routing traffic |
| container memory is close to a hard limit | `readiness` or diagnostics | choose explicitly based on operational policy |


Do not make external dependencies or ordinary CPU pressure liveness-critical unless your platform should restart the process for that failure. Readiness is usually the safer response.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/guides/payload/

Payload integration lives in a separate package and declares `payload` as a peer dependency.



```ts title="src/lib/health.ts"

export const health = createHealthManager({
  service: { name: "cms" },
  runtime: "auto",
  checks: [
    payloadHealthCheck(payload, {
      collection: "users",
      limit: 1,
      depth: 0,
    }),
  ],
});
```

`payloadHealthCheck` reports latency, document total when available, and `up`. Without `expectedMinDocuments`, an empty collection remains healthy when the query succeeds. With a minimum, `totalDocs` must be numeric and meet the floor.


Use a small `limit`, `depth: 0`, and a narrowly scoped `where` clause if one is needed. A health check should observe a dependency, not perform business work.


`timeoutMs` is normalized by the manager as `CHECK_TIMEOUT`, but the adapter does not pass an `AbortSignal` into `payload.find`; the underlying query may continue. Keep the query small rather than treating timeout as database cancellation.

---

# /packages/healthcheck/

The core runs checks and metric collectors, normalizes failures into a stable report, and leaves runtime/framework concerns to dedicated packages.


Install the core for orchestration. Add an adapter only for runtime information, route handlers, exporters, or Payload access that your service actually uses.


## Choose an integration

 entry.family === "healthcheck")} />

## Recommended path

---

# /packages/healthcheck/quick-start/

Install the core first. The `runtime: "auto"` option uses the generic runtime adapter and is appropriate when you do not need Node-specific or Bun-specific probes.





1. Create one manager per process or service boundary.

   ```ts title="src/lib/health.ts"
   import {
     createHealthManager,
     memoryCheck,
     shutdownCheck,
   } from "@nexload-sdk/healthcheck";

   export const health = createHealthManager({
     service: { name: "api" },
     runtime: "auto",
     checks: [shutdownCheck(), memoryCheck()],
   });
   ```

2. Run the scope that matches the consumer.

   ```ts
   const report = await health.run("readiness");
   console.log(report.status);
   ```



## Add an external dependency

Use `httpCheck` for an HTTP dependency. Dependencies belong in readiness by default because their failure should normally stop traffic, not restart the process.

```ts

health.register(httpCheck("billing", "https://billing.internal/health"));
```


Adding database, cache, or remote HTTP failures to liveness can cause restart loops during an upstream outage. Keep liveness focused on process lifecycle unless that restart behavior is explicitly desired.

---

# /packages/payload-editor/extensions/

```ts

export const editor = createEditor({
  preset: "article",
  extendFeatures: [BlocksFeature({ blocks: [Callout, Gallery] })],
});
```

Native providers keep their input order and append after managed features. Missing keys and managed/native or native/native duplicate keys throw before Payload's last-wins behavior can hide the collision.

To replace a managed feature, disable it in `features`, then append the native replacement. Payload remains responsible for dependency and priority sorting during sanitization.

Code blocks use Payload's `BlocksFeature` plus the project-owned Blocks schema. AI and themes have no stable package interface.

---

# /packages/payload-editor/features/

Feature values have four useful states: absence inherits the preset, `false` disables, `true` enables or resets to adapter defaults, and an options object shallow-merges over preset options. Nested arrays replace; `null` is rejected.

Managed boolean features are `paragraph`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strikethrough`, `inlineCode`, `unorderedList`, `orderedList`, `blockquote`, `horizontalRule`, `inlineToolbar`, and `fixedToolbar`.

Options map as follows:

| Semantic option | Payload option |
| --- | --- |
| `heading.sizes` | `enabledHeadingSizes` |
| `allowedCollections` | `enabledCollections` |
| `link.autoLink: false` | `disableAutoLinks: true` |
| relational `maxDepth` | native `maxDepth` |

`maxDepth: 0` is valid. Presets use `1`; larger values must be an explicit consumer choice. Upload sub-fields, link fields, exclusions, and Blocks use a native replacement or extension rather than expanding the semantic interface.

---

# /packages/payload-editor/

`@nexload-sdk/payload-editor` provides one explicit server-side configuration seam. It owns semantic features, preset contracts, validation, deterministic resolution, and translation to official Payload features.

It does not own rich-text fields, frontend rendering, Blocks schemas, AI actions, themes, or Payload feature dependency sorting.

<div class="doc-card-grid">




</div>

---

# /packages/payload-editor/migration/

1. Match `payload` and `@payloadcms/richtext-lexical` exactly within Payload 3.
2. Choose the closest explicit preset or provide a complete `features` definition.
3. Translate collection allowlists to `allowedCollections` and keep upload sub-fields native.
4. Move project Blocks and custom providers to `extendFeatures`.
5. Disable a managed feature before adding a native replacement with the same key.
6. Verify root and field editors through a real Payload config build.

Do not migrate ambiguous `code` to a managed feature: use `inlineCode` for inline formatting and native Blocks for code blocks. There is no CJS, AI, theme, `defaultFeatures`, `rootFeatures`, or advanced engine export.

---

# /packages/payload-editor/presets/

Built-in names describe authoring tasks: `compact`, `standard`, `structured-content`, `article`, and `product-description`. There is no hidden default.

- `compact`: paragraph, bold, italic, link, inline toolbar.
- `standard`: compact formatting plus underline, lists, blockquote, and fixed toolbar.
- `structured-content`: headings `h2`–`h4`, extended formatting, lists, divider, upload, and both toolbars.
- `article`: structured content with `h5`, inline code, and relationship.
- `product-description`: headings `h2`–`h3`, core formatting, lists, upload, and both toolbars.

Relational features in presets use `maxDepth: 1`.

```ts

const landing = defineEditorPreset({
  features: { paragraph: true, heading: { sizes: ["h2"] }, bold: true },
});

export const editor = createEditor({ preset: landing });
```

`defineEditorPreset` validates and snapshots input. Changing an existing built-in preset contract requires a major release.

---

# /packages/payload-editor/quick-start/

`payload` and all installed `@payloadcms/*` packages must use the exact same version within the supported `>=3.68.5 <4` range.

```ts

export const editor = createEditor({
  preset: "structured-content",
  features: {
    heading: { sizes: ["h2", "h3"] },
    upload: { allowedCollections: ["media"], maxDepth: 1 },
  },
});
```

Use the returned value as Payload's root `editor` or a `richText` field editor. `createEditor()` without an explicit preset or features definition is invalid.

---

# /packages/payload-editor/reference-api/

Public types include `CreateEditorOptions`, `EditorFeatureConfig`, `EditorPreset`, `EditorPresetName`, `HeadingSize`, option types, `NativeEditorFeature`, and `PayloadEditorConfigErrorCode`.

The root is ESM-only and server/config safe. Registry, adapter, merge, order, and resolver internals are not exported.

---

# /packages/payload-fields/

Payload Fields owns both the server field definition and the matching Admin component contract. It is designed for Payload CMS applications that need consistent Unicode slugs, Jalali date experiences, and safe money persistence.

## Choose a field contract









Money values in REST, GraphQL, Local API, hooks, validation, and persistence are minor-unit integers. Only the Admin input accepts major-unit text.

---

# /packages/payload-fields/jalali-dates/

`jalaliDateField` persists a normal Payload date. Jalali behavior belongs to input and presentation, not to a second storage format.



    ```ts
    import { jalaliDateField } from "@nexload-sdk/payload-fields";

    jalaliDateField({
      name: "publishedAt",
      pickerAppearance: "dayOnly",
      display: { timeZone: "Asia/Tehran" },
    });
    ```


    ```ts
    import { withJalaliTimestamps } from "@nexload-sdk/payload-fields";

    fields: withJalaliTimestamps([
      { name: "title", type: "text" },
    ]);
    ```



## Picker modes

| Appearance | Persistence behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `dayOnly` | canonical 12:00 date value |
| `monthOnly` | first Jalali day at canonical 12:00 |
| `dayAndTime` | calendar and local time controls; test date-change time preservation for your flow |
| `timeOnly` | edits the existing date context; empty-state baseline currently uses the browser clock |

`withJalaliTimestamps` adds read-only virtual text fields in `afterRead`; it does not store duplicate timestamp data. Duplicate virtual names are configuration errors.


`display.timeZone` controls display formatting. It does not replace Payload's own timezone configuration or change what the native date field stores.


Canonical noon and time controls use the browser/runtime local timezone. The current Admin component relies on native number inputs for hour/minute bounds, and selecting a new calendar day can replace previously edited time. Treat these as integration caveats and add component tests before relying on stricter behavior.

---

# /packages/payload-fields/migration/

1. Replace positional slug calls with an options object.

   ```diff lang="ts"
   - ...slugField("title")
   + ...slugField({ source: "title" })
   ```

2. Replace older date helpers with `jalaliDateField({ name })`.

3. Migrate decimal price storage to integer minor units before switching fields.

4. Remove `editor` usage. It is not exported by this major version; a separate `payload-editor` package is not part of this release.




Update REST, GraphQL, Local API clients, hooks, fixtures, and integrations together. A stored value is now an integer minor-unit amount, not a decimal major-unit value.

---

# /packages/payload-fields/money/

`moneyField` creates a Payload `number` field whose server-side value is always a safe integer minor-unit amount.

```ts

moneyField({
  name: "price",
  currency: "IRT",
  minMinorUnits: 0,
});
```



    ```ts
    import { parseMoneyToMinorUnits } from "@nexload-sdk/payload-fields";

    const value = parseMoneyToMinorUnits("۱۲٬۵۰۰", "IRT");
    ```


    ```ts
    import { formatMoney } from "@nexload-sdk/payload-fields";

    const label = formatMoney(12500, "IRT");
    ```



## Contract

- REST, GraphQL, Local API, hooks, validation, and persistence use integer minor units.
- The Admin field is the only UI boundary that accepts a major-unit string.
- Floating point, unsafe integers, unsupported precision, and negative values are rejected unless `allowNegative` is enabled.
- `IRR` and `IRT` both have zero fraction digits.


Calling `parseMoneyToMinorUnits` is an explicit decision at an input boundary. Do not convert arbitrary server API values from major units automatically.

---

# /packages/payload-fields/plugin-and-admin/

The root package exports server-safe factories and helpers. Factory return values contain the package-owned Admin component paths needed by Payload's Import Map system.



- src
  - payload.config.ts
  - collections
    - Posts.ts
  - app
    - (payload)
      - admin
        - importMap.js



## Plugin endpoint

`payloadFieldsPlugin({ slugGenerators, generateSlugAccess })` adds `POST /payload-fields/generate-slug`.

- Authentication is required before the endpoint evaluates custom access.
- Request bodies must be non-null objects with the registered generator key and string source value.
- Generator lookup accepts only explicitly registered own keys; inherited prototype names are rejected.
- A registered generator receives source text and the Payload request on the server.
- The response is `{ slug }` or `{ error: { code, message } }`.
- The final generated value is normalized with `formatSlug`.


Consumer overrides may extend supported field options, hooks, metadata, and slots. They must not replace the semantic field type, required component path, or protected name contract.

---

# /packages/payload-fields/quick-start/

1. Add the factories to your collection fields.

   ```ts title="src/collections/Posts.ts"
   import {
     jalaliDateField,
     moneyField,
     slugField,
   } from "@nexload-sdk/payload-fields";

   export const Posts = {
     slug: "posts",
     fields: [
       { name: "title", type: "text", required: true },
       ...slugField({ source: "title" }),
       jalaliDateField({ name: "publishedAt" }),
       moneyField({ name: "price", currency: "IRT" }),
     ],
   };
   ```

2. Add `payloadFieldsPlugin()` only when a slug uses a registered remote or AI generator.



Each factory protects the semantic field type, name, and package-owned Admin component. Use `overrides` for supported consumer configuration instead of replacing those boundaries.

---

# /packages/payload-fields/reference-api/



---

# /packages/payload-fields/slug/

`slugField()` returns a slug `TextField` and its paired lock `CheckboxField`. Add both to the collection with the spread operator.

```ts

fields: [
  { name: "title", type: "text", localized: true },
  ...slugField({
    source: "title",
    overrides: { slug: { localized: true } },
  }),
];
```

## Synchronization rules

- Persian and other Unicode letters are preserved; Arabic variants and digits are normalized.
- The lock field is localized when the slug is localized.
- A locked slug regenerates only when its non-empty source changes.
- Clearing a source with an empty string or `null` preserves the exact previous slug.
- `formatSlug` is the final normalization authority.

## Registered generators



1. Register an async server-side generator in `payloadFieldsPlugin`.

   ```ts
   import { payloadFieldsPlugin } from "@nexload-sdk/payload-fields";

   export default buildConfig({
     plugins: [
       payloadFieldsPlugin({
         slugGenerators: {
           concise: async ({ sourceValue }) => sourceValue,
         },
       }),
     ],
   });
   ```

2. Reference its key from the field definition with `generator: "concise"`.




Only the generator key reaches client props. The implementation remains on the server; the plugin checks authentication before access policy, rejects malformed/non-object input, resolves only own registered generator keys, and applies final `formatSlug` normalization.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/architecture/

Factories create immutable public definitions backed by private symbol state. `defineEntity` validates and normalizes that state into a closure-owned IR; neither the IR nor compiler is exported.

```text
field factory → immutable definition → defineEntity
  ├─ payload facade → fresh Payload field configs
  ├─ schema context → canonical Zod contracts
  └─ inspect → safe deterministic metadata
```

Canonical schemas own intrinsic type checks, constraints, and same-type normalization. Payload owns required-field presence, persistence, collection lifecycle, access, drafts, localization, and populated documents. Application schemas own cross-field and use-case rules.

Each schema-capable compiled field receives one server-side `beforeValidate` adapter. Consumer `beforeValidate` hooks run first; the canonical adapter runs last and returns the parsed value. Group and array parents validate only container shape and row limits because Payload traverses children separately.

Every `payload.all()`, `payload.pick()`, and `payload.field()` call deep-clones plain containers by descriptor. Functions, editors, components, regular expressions, maps, sets, and class instances remain opaque references; getters are not executed while cloning.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/errors/

`PayloadSchemaError` is reserved for developer/configuration failures. Its code union is exactly `keyof PayloadSchemaErrorDataMap`; phases are `definition`, `payload-compilation`, `schema-derivation`, and `internal`.

Common codes include `INVALID_FIELD_CONFIGURATION`, `INVALID_DEFAULT_VALUE`, `CONFLICTING_DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION`, `RESERVED_PAYLOAD_OPTION`, `INVALID_PAYLOAD_FIELD`, `UNKNOWN_FIELD`, `SCHEMA_UNAVAILABLE`, and `ASYNC_CANONICAL_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`.

```ts
try {
  defineProductEntity();
} catch (error) {
  if (isPayloadSchemaError(error, "INVALID_DEFAULT_VALUE")) {
    console.error(error.data.fieldPath, error.data.issues);
  }
}
```

`toJSON()` includes only name, code, phase, message, and safe data. It excludes stack, cause, raw values, schemas, functions, complete config, and secrets.

Invalid field data flowing through Payload becomes Payload's `ValidationError`, not `PayloadSchemaError`.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/fields/

| Factory | Payload type | Canonical value |
|---|---|---|
| `field.text`, `field.textarea` | text / textarea | string with trim, case, length, and pattern rules |
| `field.slug` | text | NFKC normalized lowercase slug |
| `field.number` | number | finite number with integer, safe, range, and multiple rules |
| `field.money` | number | safe integer; currency is inspection metadata |
| `field.boolean` | checkbox | boolean |
| `field.date` | date | timezone-qualified datetime normalized to UTC ISO |
| `field.select` | select | literal union or array of literals |
| `field.relationship`, `field.upload` | relationship / upload | ID or polymorphic `{ relationTo, value }` reference |
| `field.group` | group | strict recursive object when every descendant has a schema |
| `field.array` | array | strict recursive object rows without Payload row IDs |
| `field.richText` | richText | consumer-provided Zod schema |
| `field.native` | native data field | optional consumer-provided Zod schema |

`defaultValue` is static, parsed at entity definition, and copied to Payload without adding `.default()` to Zod. `dynamicDefaultValue` is a native Payload function forwarded opaquely. Setting both is invalid. `payload.defaultValue` is always reserved.

Text transforms run in fixed order: type, trim, case, length, pattern, customizer. Date bounds compare instants. Populated relationship documents are never accepted by canonical relationship schemas.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/

`@nexload-sdk/payload-schema` owns intrinsic field validation and normalization. One entity definition compiles fresh Payload fields and exposes the same canonical Zod schemas for application contracts.

It does not create collections, infer CRUD DTOs, model populated relationships, own authorization, or replace Payload-generated persistence types.

<div class="doc-card-grid">




</div>

---

# /packages/payload-schema/migration/

1. Choose one small field group with duplicated Payload and Zod rules.
2. Define those intrinsic rules with `field.*` factories.
3. Replace only the corresponding native collection entries with `entity.payload.pick(...)`.
4. Rebuild existing input or output schemas through `entity.schema(...)`.
5. Verify Local API writes, generated Payload types, and existing hooks before expanding the migration.

Keep collection access, hooks, tabs, uploads, drafts, localization, and business workflows in their current Payload owners. Use `field.native` for unsupported data fields; keep layout fields directly in the collection.

Static defaults move to factory-level `defaultValue`. Dynamic Payload defaults move to `dynamicDefaultValue`. Never copy defaults into Zod `.default()` unless a specific consumer contract independently requires that behavior.

Migration is reversible: compiled fields remain ordinary Payload field configs and canonical schemas remain ordinary Zod schemas.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/native-fields/

Use `field.native` for data-affecting Payload types not covered by a built-in factory.

```ts

const location = field.native({
  payload: { type: "point" },
  schema: z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()]),
});
```

Without `schema`, the field still compiles for Payload but is omitted from the schema context. A group or array containing it also becomes schema-unavailable; the picker reports the first blocking descendant path. Static defaults require a schema, while `dynamicDefaultValue` remains allowed.

Layout and UI fields such as rows, tabs, and collapsibles do not represent entity data and are rejected. Compose those directly in the Payload collection around `entity.payload.pick(...)`.

Native `validate` and hooks remain consumer-owned. The package only appends its canonical hook when a schema exists.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/payload-integration/

The entity is not a collection builder. Keep collection lifecycle and layout native:

```ts
export const Products = {
  slug: "products",
  hooks: { beforeChange: [applyBusinessRules] },
  fields: [
    { type: "tabs", tabs: [
      { label: "Content", fields: productEntity.payload.pick(["title", "slug"]) },
      { label: "Stock", fields: productEntity.payload.pick(["inventory"]) },
    ] },
  ],
};
```

The canonical adapter is a server-side field `beforeValidate` hook. It passes `undefined` through for Payload required/default handling, returns normalized valid values, and converts Zod issues to Payload `ValidationError` entries with dot paths such as `gallery.0.alt`.

Consumer field hooks are cloned and preserved. Consumer `beforeValidate` hooks run before the package adapter. Native `validate` is not replaced or translated.

Keep all Payload and `@payloadcms/*` packages on the same exact version. Payload-generated types remain authoritative for persisted documents.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/projections/

Canonical relationship fields accept IDs only. A populated document is a consumer output concern:

```ts
const productCardSchema = productEntity.schema(({ fields, z }) =>
  z.object({
    id: productEntity.idSchema,
    title: fields.title,
    category: z.object({ id: z.union([z.string(), z.number()]), title: z.string() }),
  }),
);
```

Keep projections small and named by use case. Validate external or serialized output at its boundary. Do not treat `InferEntityFields` as a persisted document model; it describes canonical field values only.

This separation prevents Payload population depth, access behavior, and generated document types from leaking into reusable field definitions.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/quick-start/

Supported versions are Node `>=20.9.0`, Payload `>=3.85.0 <4`, and Zod `>=4 <5`.

```ts

export const productEntity = defineEntity({
  name: "Product",
  fields: {
    title: field.text({ required: true, trim: true }),
    slug: field.slug({ required: true }),
    inventory: field.number({ integer: true, safe: true, defaultValue: 0 }),
  },
});

export const Products = {
  slug: "products",
  fields: productEntity.payload.all(),
};
```

Build application contracts explicitly:

```ts
export const createProductSchema = productEntity.schema(({ pick }) =>
  pick(["title", "slug", "inventory"], { optional: ["inventory"] }),
);
```

---

# /packages/payload-schema/reference-api/

Stable root types include all entity, field option, inference, inspection, picker, and error-contract types. Compiler, IR, registry, adapter internals, and deep imports are not public.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/schema-derivation/

`entity.schema` accepts any Zod result, including primitives, transforms, codecs, unions, tuples, arrays, and objects.

```ts
const searchSchema = productEntity.schema(({ fields, z }) =>
  z.object({ query: fields.title.optional() }).transform(({ query }) => query ?? ""),
);
```

`pick` is strict by default and preserves caller key order. Selected properties are required unless explicitly made optional. Nullability comes from the field schema and is independent of property presence.

```ts
const patchSchema = productEntity.schema(({ pick }) =>
  pick(["title", "inventory"], {
    optional: "all",
    required: ["title"],
  }),
);
```

Schema-less fields are absent from the typed context. Untyped JavaScript calls receive `UNKNOWN_FIELD` or `SCHEMA_UNAVAILABLE` rather than silently dropping data.

Arbitrary schemas returned from `entity.schema` may be async. Canonical field schemas must be synchronous; async behavior is reported when synchronous parsing first encounters a Promise.

---

# /packages/payload-schema/testing-compatibility/

| Runtime | Minimum lane | Current lane |
|---|---:|---:|
| Node.js | 20.9.0 | 22 |
| Payload | 3.85.0 | 3.86.0 |
| Zod | 4.0.0 | 4.4.3 |
| PostgreSQL | 18 | 18 |

Pull requests exercise the minimum and current lanes. Main, release tags, and manual runs exercise the full Payload/Zod cross-product. Every `@payloadcms/*` dependency in a lane matches Payload exactly.

Package verification includes public-interface unit tests, TypeScript inference tests, SQLite boot and persistence, PostgreSQL relationships and IDs, generated Payload types, and a packed independent consumer. The tarball test checks runtime imports, declarations, exports, config compilation, and rejection of deep imports.

Canonical schema learning tests lock public Payload/Zod behavior at both supported edges rather than relying on private library internals.

# /start/choose-a-package/

## Choose by problem

| You need to… | Start with | Add when needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| expose service probes and reports | `@nexload-sdk/healthcheck` | Node, Bun, Next.js, Payload, Prometheus, or OpenTelemetry adapters |
| ship a Node or container health endpoint | `@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-node` | `@nexload-sdk/healthcheck-next` for App Router routes |
| build Payload fields with Persian-aware UI | `@nexload-sdk/payload-fields` | its generated Admin Import Map subpaths |
| standardize Payload Lexical editor configuration | `@nexload-sdk/payload-editor` | native extensions for project-owned features and Blocks |
| reuse canonical field validation across Payload and application contracts | `@nexload-sdk/payload-schema` | native fields for unsupported data types and layout fields outside entities |
| validate environment configuration | `@nexload-sdk/env` | Docs planned |
| use structured logs | `@nexload-sdk/logger` | Docs planned |
| create policy-driven JWTs | `@nexload-sdk/jwt` | Docs planned |

## Fully documented paths








Packages marked `Docs planned` remain available from npm and their package README, but do not yet receive a minimal overview page in this site.

---

# /start/introduction/

Nexload SDK is not a single application framework. Each package has a narrow ownership boundary and can be installed independently.

## Package families









## Selection rule

Choose the package closest to the responsibility you need. For example, use the Healthcheck core to aggregate health results, then add the Node adapter only when you need cgroup, TCP, DNS, or process data.


The Healthcheck core intentionally does not import Next.js, Payload, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Bun, `ping`, or `systeminformation`. Add the integration package at the application boundary.


## What these docs guarantee

Documented pages describe the current source and public exports of the latest package version. Migration pages cover supported major-version changes; historical versioned documentation is not maintained.
